title: Battery cathode leaching: ultrasound, controls and measurements

steps.title: Exclude a literature conditions table
steps.question: Why is this table not a current-study result?
steps.look: Gate skips the table of cited leaching conditions. The current experiment’s outcomes are extracted from text instead.
steps.boundary: A skipped table does not imply that the paper has no useful recovery evidence.

where.table_id: TABLE_Ultrasound-Assisted Leaching of Cobalt and Lithium from Spent Lithium-Ion Batteries_0001

steps.title: Identify ultrasound-assisted leaching
steps.question: What treatment did this study perform?
steps.look: Process discovery records ultrasound-assisted leaching of Co and Li from calcined cathode material.
steps.boundary: This is the prepared cathode feed, not an untreated complete battery.

where.name: ultrasound-assisted leaching of Co and Li from calcined cathode materials

steps.title: Keep the conventional control distinct
steps.question: What is the comparison treatment?
steps.look: The archive separately records conventional leaching without ultrasound assistance.
steps.boundary: A common metal target does not make the two treatment routes identical.

where.name: conventional leaching of Co and Li from calcined cathode materials

steps.title: Distinguish a kinetic parameter from recovery
steps.question: Is 3.8482 kJ/mol a recovery percentage?
steps.look: The reviewed archive retains 3.8482 kJ/mol as a Co kinetic measurement in Revision / Postprocessing, outside the material-output graph.
steps.boundary: A fitted kinetic parameter is evidence about a process, not an amount or recovery of its material output.

steps.title: Attach method scope after extraction
steps.question: Which method family contextualizes this process?
steps.look: Scope annotates the existing ultrasound-assisted Process using archived evidence. It does not create another treatment result.
steps.boundary: Method scope is not an assertion that every battery or catalog model was tested.

where.scope_subject_text: ultrasound-assisted leaching of Co and Li from calcined cathode material

steps.title: Read the cobalt outcome with its conditions
steps.question: What does the reported 94.63% apply to?
steps.look: The optimized ultrasound-assisted treatment reports 94.63% Co leaching: 2 M H2SO4, 5% H2O2, 100 g/L, 360 W, 30 minutes and 30 °C.
steps.boundary: Leaching efficiency is not final metal-product purity, and it must not be pooled with other treatment conditions.

where.evidence_span: Optimal leaching efficiency of 94.63% for cobalt, and 98.62% for lithium, respectively, was achieved by using 2M H2SO4 with 5% (v/v) H2O2 at a solid/liquid ratio of 100 g/L, and an ultrasonic power of 360 W, and the leaching time being 30 min under 30 ℃.

steps.title: Read lithium from the same reported treatment
steps.question: Does the same treatment have one universal recovery value?
steps.look: The same optimized treatment reports 98.62% Li leaching, separately from the Co result.

where.evidence_span: Optimal leaching efficiency of 94.63% for cobalt, and 98.62% for lithium, respectively, was achieved by using 2M H2SO4 with 5% (v/v) H2O2 at a solid/liquid ratio of 100 g/L, and an ultrasonic power of 360 W, and the leaching time being 30 min under 30 ℃.

steps.title: Trace the treatment in the fused graph
steps.question: Can an industry user inspect the evidence behind an outcome?
steps.look: Open this Process’s HAS_OUTPUT observations and return to the source through View evidence in replay.
steps.boundary: The graph connects evidence; it does not recommend optimal conditions for an untested battery feed.
